title: Secretary of State of Arkansas

context.text: The seat is open. Kim Hammer won the March 31, 2026 Republican runoff over Bryan Norris by 913 votes of 80,977 cast; recounts in six counties matched the original totals and a lawsuit challenging the Saline County results was dismissed on June 8. Kelly Grappe was unopposed for the Democratic nomination.

candidates.name: Kelly Grappe
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the Democratic primary, which was canceled.

priorities.text: Restoring confidence through transparent, professional election administration, with better voter education and training for election workers.
Modernizing the office's business services and expanding civic education.

candidates.researchNotes: She has not held elected office.

candidates.name: Kim Hammer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 31, 2026 Republican primary runoff by 913 votes.

record.text: Chaired the Senate Efficiency Committee in the 2025-2026 session and also sat on the Senate Revenue and Taxation and State Agencies and Governmental Affairs committees.

candidates.researchNotes: He has not completed Ballotpedia's survey and no 2026 campaign materials were found, so no priorities or positions are listed; legislative votes were not researched.

priorities.text: Eliminating partisan gerrymandering, reforming primaries and opening the process for independent and third-party candidates.
Considering alternative voting systems such as ranked-choice voting.

sources.title: Arkansas Secretary of State election, 2026 — Candidate Connection survey

researchNotes: Slate from Ballotpedia, cross-checked against The Green Papers' Arkansas candidate list (Grappe, Hammer, Pakko). The Arkansas Secretary of State's candidate search is a script-driven page that could not be read, so the slate rests on Ballotpedia, which warns the list may not be complete. No direct statement on documentary proof of citizenship was found from any candidate.
